question.problem: In a microchip factory, each chip is tested for defects before being packaged. On average, $6$ out of every $200$ chips are defective. The chips are tested one by one until a defective chip is found. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that a defective chip will be found before testing the $5$th chip is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of chips tested until a defective chip is found. On average, the chance of finding a defective chip on any single test is 

$$
p=\frac{6}{200}=0.03.
$$

So, the number of chips that are tested until a defective chip is found can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.03.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.03).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.03)^{x-1}(0.03) \\  & =(0.97)^{x-1}(0.03)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding a defective chip before testing the $5$th chip is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.97)^{1-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{2-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{3-1}(0.03)+(0.97)^{4-1}(0.03) \\  & =(0.03)+(0.97)(0.03)+(0.97)^{2}(0.03)+(0.97)^{3}(0.03) \\  & =[1+0.97+(0.97)^{2}+(0.97)^{3}](0.03) \\  & ≈0.115,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
